title: SOCIALHARMBENCH: REVEALING LLM VULNERABILITIES TO SOCIALLY HARMFUL REQUESTS

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM compliance rates on adversarial prompts requesting assistance with high-stakes sociopolitical harms, including political manipulation, propaganda generation, censorship, and historical revisionism using automated classifiers (HarmBench and StrongREJECT).

Comparing model attack success rates (ASR) and refusal robustness across prompts contextualized in 34 different countries and regions (e.g., Latin America, USA, UK, Europe, Africa) to identify region-specific vulnerabilities.
Measuring variations in harmful compliance and refusal rates when prompts are framed around different historical time periods (e.g., pre-20th century, 20th century, and 21st century).

Testing model susceptibility to generating harmful content involving systematic oppression, persecution, and surveillance targeting specific ethnic and religious groups to evaluate inherent partisan bias.
